exec: The NSA says a disruption to its classified network came during scheduled routine maintenance and that mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational.
impact: CNN reported staggered arrivals for personnel; an NSA spokesman said mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational.
plain: The classified internal network used by US National Security Agency staff went down or ran intermittently from November 17. An NSA spokesperson says it is now operating under normal conditions; CNN's sources said there was no evidence of a cyberattack.

sources.name: New Turkish Post (Arabic): outage enters third day

summary: CNN reported, citing six people, that NSA Net went down on 17 November; other sources say service was intermittent. The NSA cites degradation during scheduled routine maintenance; DNI Jay Clayton linked it to PHP patching. CNN's sources said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. On 20 November an NSA spokesperson told Nextgov: "NSA can confirm that we are now operating under normal conditions."
title: NSA's classified internal network NSA Net goes down

validation.note: Agency statement plus several outlets; extent of the outage is described differently by different sources. The Record's second-day report (read) cites one unnamed source for the network working and restoration taking a day or two. Nextgov (read 21 Nov, published 20 Nov) quotes an NSA spokesperson confirming normal conditions.

review.note: Compared with Nextgov, The Record, WRAL, USA Today: summary matches; exec stated maintenance cause as fact, now attributed to the NSA statement
